name: Lamb Chops with Mash and Peas
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut into even chunks. Boil in a large pot of salted water for about 15 minutes, until tender when pierced with a knife.
Drain the potatoes well and return them to the hot pot. Mash with the milk and 40 g of the butter until smooth, season with salt and pepper, then cover to keep warm.
While the potatoes cook, pat the lamb chops dry, rub with the crushed garlic and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chops for 4-5 minutes each side for medium, or longer to your liking.
Move the chops to a plate, cover loosely with foil and rest for 5 minutes.
While the chops rest, tip the peas into a saucepan with the remaining 20 g butter and a splash of water. Cook over medium heat, stirring, for 3-4 minutes until hot.
Stir the chopped mint through the peas with a good squeeze of lemon juice, and season to taste.
Pile the mash onto plates, top with the lamb chops, spoon the peas alongside and serve with the rest of the lemon cut into wedges.
